explanation.text: The claim that Spain ceded Louisiana to the United States on April 30, 1803, is contradicted by the evidence. Spain ceded Louisiana to France via the Third Treaty of San Ildefonso in 1800, and France later ceded it to the United States through the Louisiana Purchase, completed in late 1803.
The treaty signing occurred in 1800 (Third Treaty of San Ildefonso), not April 30, 1803 as claimed.
The 1803 transfer from France to the United States took place on December 20, 1803, not April 30, 1803.

excerpts.text: In 1801, Spanish Governor Don [Juan Manuel de Salcedo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Manuel_de_Salcedo "Juan Manuel de Salcedo") took over from the [Marquess of Casa Calvo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_colonial_governors_of_Louisiana#Spanish_period "List of colonial governors of Louisiana"), and restored the American right to deposit goods. However, in 1800, Spain had ceded the Louisiana territory back to France as part of Napoleon's secret [Third Treaty of San Ildefonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Treaty_of_San_Ildefonso "Third Treaty of San Ildefonso").[[8]](#cite_note-10) The subsequent 1801 [Treaty of Aranjuez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Aranjuez_(1801) "Treaty of Aranjuez (1801)") established that Spain's cession of Louisiana was a "restoration" of the territory to France, not a retrocession.[[9]](#cite_note-Chambers-11) The territory nominally remained under Spanish control, until a transfer of power to France on November 30, 1803, just three weeks before the formal cession of the territory to the United States on December 20, 1803.[[10]](#cite_note-12)

excerpts.text: In the Third Treaty of San Ildefonso Spain secretly traded [**the colony of Louisiana**](https://64parishes.org/entry/spanish-colonial-louisiana) to France on October 1, 1800.
In April 1803 he instructed French Foreign Minister François Barbé-Marbois to sell the entire territory of Louisiana to the United States.
The Treaty of San Ildefonso briefly returned Louisiana to France, but the Spanish continued to govern the territory until late 1803.
Laussat formally governed the territory for three weeks, overseeing a peaceful transfer from Spain to France on November 30 and from France to the United States on December 20, 1803.
